fullPassage:
[1번] People often omit the period at the end of sentences in single-sentence text messages, which has influenced the way we perceive periods. In an experiment, participants reading text messages found single sentences with a period less sincere than those without one. This could be due to something called "situational code-switching," which simply means that we change how we talk depending on the social setting. For example, the language that students use in the classroom is different from the language they use on the playground. If they talked to their friends the same way they talked to their teachers, it would probably sound strange. Similarly, a person using periods in text messages can cause feelings of awkwardness, just like someone using formal language in a casual setting.

[2번] In the 1800s, the people of Ireland used potatoes as their basic food source. Unfortunately, everyone was growing the same type of potato, which meant the crops all had the same genes. The farmers did not realize the danger in this. In the 1840s, a new potato disease struck. The genetically identical potatoes all lacked the ability to fight the disease, so they all rotted. Because people were dependent mainly on potatoes for their food, Ireland suffered a famine in which one in eight people died during the following years. If people had grown many types of potatoes, they could have identified resistant ones and grown more of them, making the famine less serious. Despite knowing this, many countries today take the same risk with their crops.

[3번] In 1985, my husband and I moved to his hometown, located in China's Ordas Desert. When I first saw our new home, I burst into tears. There was nothing but sand for miles around. "I wish I could see some plants," I thought. Then one day I saw a small tree growing beside a nearby well. I realized that if this tree could survive, others might be able to, too. I started to plant more trees. At first, many of them ended up buried in sandstorms, but my husband and I eventually managed to get most of the trees to survive. We have now planted more than 600,000 trees in the desert. We have turned one of the most desolate places in China into something beautiful.

[4번] Socotra Island, a small island owned by Yemen and located in the Arabian Sea, looks as if it were part of another planet. In fact, it separated from the mainland of Africa six or seven million years ago, causing unique forms of life to develop on it. It is home to about 800 species of rare plants and animals, many of which are found nowhere else on earth. Because the island experiences extreme heat and frequent droughts, many of its plants have evolved unusual appearances. One striking example is the dragon's blood tree. Its branches make it look like a giant umbrella. It gets its name from a thick, red substance that comes out when its bark is cut. When this happens, it appears as if the tree were bleeding.

[5번] Everyone on Earth may soon lose one second of time. For the first time ever, scientists are considering subtracting a single second. This is called a "negative leap second," and it may be necessary in 2029 because Earth is rotating slightly faster than before. Surprisingly, without global warming, this time change would likely have been necessary sooner. The reason Earth is spinning faster is the unpredictable behavior of its hot liquid core. This behavior has been causing an increase in speed for approximately 50 years, but the melting of polar ice has been counteracting this effect. Melting ice raises sea levels and shifts the planet's mass away from the poles and toward the equator. This slows the Earth's rotation in the same way that figure skaters spin more slowly when extending their arms outward. Without the melting of polar ice, it is likely that we would need to lose a second in 2026 rather than 2029. "We are headed toward a negative leap second," said one expert. "It's a matter of when."

[6번] The origins of flags probably began with warriors decorating their spears with colored ribbons as a way of distinguishing one army from another. This practice was adopted by early explorers, who started using flags to show who newly discovered lands belonged to. During the modern era, flags became a symbol of individual nations, and it has become accepted that every country must have its own flag. Most of these national flags are roughly the same size and shape. They commonly feature bold colors and simple patterns, as flags with intricate patterns would appear distorted when blowing in the wind.

[7번] Around 2.35 billion years ago, Earth's atmosphere underwent a significant transition: It went from being oxygen-free to possessing a small percentage of oxygen. This change was partly due to tiny organisms known as cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria, which evolved approximately 2.7 billion years ago, took in water to obtain hydrogen. This allowed them to assimilate carbon from CO₂ in the atmosphere. They then released oxygen as waste. But how could such tiny creatures have caused such a huge change in the planet? It is believed that the amount of oxygen cyanobacteria released slowly increased over hundreds of millions of years. Over this period, it accumulated in Earth's oceans, oxygenating the water. Eventually, the oceans' accumulated oxygen began to escape into the atmosphere. There, it reacted with methane, gradually displacing it. Had there been no cyanobacteria, oxygen might never have become a major component of Earth's atmosphere.

[8번] Being alone makes us more creative. Many great artists and thinkers throughout history have lived by themselves. When we are alone, we have fewer distractions. This allows our thoughts to run free without interruption or judgment. Creative people have entire worlds inside their heads, and being alone gives them the opportunity to bring ideas from this inner world into the real world. Steve Wozniak, for example, invented the Apple computer sitting alone at a desk. He says his creativity came from being introverted as a child. Had it not been for his shyness, he might not have become a computer expert. However, this does not mean we should stop working together with others. Had it not been for Wozniak's collaboration with Steve Jobs, he could not have started his own business. Therefore, we should seek out solitude, but only when we need it.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: read → reading (한 문장에 본동사 found가 이미 있으므로 participants를 꾸미는 분사 reading)
det.analysis:
① read: 'participants read text messages found single sentences ~'를 보세요. 이 문장의 진짜 동사는 뒤의 found예요. 그런데 read도 동사로 보면 접속사도 없이 동사가 둘이 되어 문장이 깨져요. 그래서 앞부분은 participants를 꾸미는 현재분사 reading('~을 읽던')이어야 해요 ←정답

③ that: 'the language that students use' 관계대명사 — 적절
④ cause: 'can cause' 조동사 뒤 동사원형 — 적절

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: unique → identical (같은 품종만 길러 유전자가 '동일'했기에 다 함께 병에 졌다)

det.korean: ③ ordinary → striking. 특이한 외관의 대표 사례이므로 '인상적인(striking)'
det.analysis:
① located: '아라비아 해에 위치한(located)' 섬 — 적절

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: dark shades and complex symbols=어두운 색조와 복잡한 기호 / bold colors and simple patterns=선명한 색과 단순한 무늬 / tiny letters and hidden marks=작은 글자와 숨겨진 표시 / soft textures and dull tones=부드러운 질감과 칙칙한 색조
det.analysis:
빈칸 뒤에서 '복잡한 무늬(intricate patterns)의 깃발은 바람에 뒤틀려 보이기 때문'이라고 이유를 대요. 그러니 국기는 눈에 잘 띄고 뒤틀리지 않는 것을 특징으로 해야 해요.

① dark shades and complex symbols(어두운 색조와 복잡한 기호): '복잡한' 것은 뒤틀린다고 했으니 반대예요.

② bold colors and simple patterns(선명한 색과 단순한 무늬): 멀리서도 잘 보이고 뒤틀리지 않도록 국기가 갖추는 특징으로 딱 맞아요. ←정답

③ tiny letters and hidden marks(작은 글자와 숨겨진 표시): 잘 보여야 하는 국기와 반대예요.

④ soft textures and dull tones(부드러운 질감과 칙칙한 색조): 눈에 띄어야 하는 색과 반대예요.
det.tip: 복잡한 무늬는 뒤틀림 → 국기는 bold colors and simple patterns(선명한 색·단순한 무늬)

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ③은 원문 'escape into the atmosphere(대기로 빠져나감)'와 달리 '우주 공간으로'라 하여 불일치

ch: 지구 대기의 변화는 부분적으로 남세균에서 비롯되었다.

남세균이 없었다면 산소는 대기의 주된 성분이 되지 못했을 것이다.

④ differences between spoken and written language(구어와 문어의 차이): 교실·놀이터 예시는 근거일 뿐 주제가 아니에요.
det.tip: 마침표 인상 변화 + 상황적 코드 전환 설명 = 문장 부호가 인상을 형성한다는 것이 주제

ch: grammatical rules for using periods correctly in writing
how punctuation in texting reflects situational code-switching and shapes impressions
the historical origin of the period as a punctuation mark
differences between spoken and written language in schools

questions.passage: In the 1800s, the people of Ireland used potatoes as their basic food source. Unfortunately, everyone was growing the same type of potato, which meant the crops all had the same genes. The farmers did not realize the danger in this. In the 1840s, a new potato disease struck. The genetically identical potatoes all lacked the ability to __________, so they all rotted. Because people were dependent mainly on potatoes for their food, Ireland suffered a famine in which one in eight people died during the following years. If people had grown many types of potatoes, they could have identified resistant ones and grown more of them, making the famine less serious. Despite knowing this, many countries today take the same risk with their crops.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: spread more widely=더 널리 퍼지다 / grow much taller=훨씬 더 크게 자라다 / change their shape=모양을 바꾸다 / fight the disease=병과 싸우다
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장은 'The genetically identical potatoes all lacked the ability to ___, so they all rotted(유전적으로 동일한 감자들은 ___할 능력이 없어서 모두 썩었다)'예요. 바로 앞에 새로운 병(disease)이 덮쳤다는 내용이 나와요.

① spread more widely(더 널리 퍼지다): 감자가 스스로 퍼진다는 것은 문맥과 무관

② grow much taller(훨씬 크게 자라다): 키가 크는 능력은 썩는 것과 연결되지 않음

③ change their shape(모양을 바꾸다): 모양 변화는 병·썩음과 무관

④ fight the disease(병과 싸우다): 병과 싸울 능력이 없어서 모두 썩었다는 흐름과 정확히 일치 ←정답
det.tip: 새 병이 덮침 + 다 썩음 → 병과 싸울(fight the disease) 능력이 없었음

questions.passage: In 1985, my husband and I moved to his hometown, located in China's Ordas Desert. When I first saw our new home, I burst into tears. There was nothing but sand for miles around. "I wish I could see some plants," I thought. Then one day I saw a small tree growing beside a nearby well. I realized that if this tree could survive, others might be able to, too. I started to plant more trees. At first, many of <u>them</u> ended up buried in sandstorms, but my husband and I eventually managed to get most of the trees to survive. We have now planted more than 600,000 trees in the desert. We have turned one of the most desolate places in China into something beautiful.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 them이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: them = 앞에서 화자가 심기 시작한 (더 많은) 나무들
det.analysis:
밑줄 친 them은 앞 문장 'I started to plant more trees(나는 더 많은 나무를 심기 시작했다)'의 그 나무들을 가리켜요.

① 화자가 새로 심기 시작한 나무들: 'many of them ended up buried(그중 다수가 파묻혔다)'에서 파묻힌 대상은 화자가 심은 나무들이라 정답이에요. ←정답

② 모래폭풍들: 나무가 '모래폭풍에(in sandstorms)' 파묻힌 것이지, 파묻힌 주체는 모래폭풍이 아니에요.

③ 처음 본 작은 나무 한 그루: them은 복수(여러 그루)라 한 그루를 가리키지 않아요.

④ 우물의 물: 문맥상 파묻히는 대상이 될 수 없어요.
det.tip: I started to plant more trees. At first, many of them ~ → them = 그 (심은) 나무들

ch: 화자가 처음 본 작은 나무 한 그루

questions.passage: Socotra Island, a small island owned by Yemen and ①<u>located</u> in the Arabian Sea, looks as if it were part of another planet. In fact, it separated from the mainland of Africa six or seven million years ago, ②<u>causing</u> unique forms of life to develop on it. It is home to about 800 species of rare plants and animals, many of which are found nowhere else on earth. Because the island experiences extreme heat and frequent droughts, many of its plants have evolved unusual appearances. One striking example is the dragon's blood tree. Its branches make it ③<u>to look</u> like a giant umbrella. It gets its name from a thick, red substance that ④<u>comes</u> out when its bark is cut. When this happens, it appears as if the tree were bleeding.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: to look → look (사역동사 make 뒤에는 to 없는 원형부정사)
det.analysis:
① located: 'a small island ... located in the Arabian Sea' 섬이 바다에 '위치된' 과거분사 후치수식 — 적절

② causing: '..., causing unique forms of life to develop' 앞 절 전체를 받는 분사구문(능동) — 적절

③ to look → look: 'Its branches make it ___ like a giant umbrella'에서 make는 '~가 …하게 만들다'라는 사역동사예요. 사역동사(make) 뒤 목적격보어에는 to를 뺀 동사원형(원형부정사)이 와요. 그래서 look이 맞고 to look은 틀림 ←정답

④ comes: 'a substance that comes out' 선행사 substance가 단수라 관계사절 동사도 -s — 적절
det.tip: 사역동사 make + 목적어 + 원형부정사(look) → to를 쓰지 않음

questions.passage: Everyone on Earth may soon lose one second of time. For the first time ever, scientists are considering subtracting a single second. This is called a "negative leap second," and it may be necessary in 2029 because Earth is rotating slightly faster than before. Surprisingly, without global warming, this time change would likely have been necessary sooner. The reason Earth is spinning faster is the unpredictable behavior of its hot liquid core. This behavior has been causing an increase in speed for approximately 50 years, but the melting of polar ice has been counteracting <u>this effect</u>. Melting ice raises sea levels and shifts the planet's mass away from the poles and toward the equator. This slows the Earth's rotation in the same way that figure skaters spin more slowly when extending their arms outward. Without the melting of polar ice, it is likely that we would need to lose a second in 2026 rather than 2029. "We are headed toward a negative leap second," said one expert. "It's a matter of when."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 this effect가 가리키는 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: this effect = 앞 절의 'causing an increase in speed', 즉 핵의 활동이 자전 속도를 높여 온 것
det.analysis:
밑줄이 있는 문장은 'This behavior has been causing an increase in speed ..., but the melting of polar ice has been counteracting ① this effect(핵의 활동이 속도 증가를 일으켜 왔지만, 얼음이 녹는 것이 이 효과를 상쇄해 왔다)'예요. 얼음이 녹는 것이 상쇄하는 대상은 바로 앞의 '속도 증가'예요.

✅ ① 핵의 활동이 자전 속도를 높여 온 것 — 상쇄되는 대상인 '속도 증가'와 맞아요 ←정답

❌ ② 얼음이 녹는 현상 — 얼음이 녹는 것은 상쇄하는 '주체'이지 상쇄되는 대상이 아니에요.

❌ ③ 해수면 상승 — 뒤에 나오는 결과일 뿐, this effect가 가리키는 대상이 아니에요.

❌ ④ 질량 이동 — 역시 뒤에 이어지는 과정이에요.
det.tip: 얼음이 상쇄하는 대상 = 앞의 '속도 증가' → 핵이 자전을 빠르게 한 것

ch: 뜨거운 액체 핵의 활동이 지구의 자전 속도를 높여 온 것
극지방의 얼음이 빠르게 녹고 있는 현상
지구의 질량이 적도 쪽으로 이동하는 현상

questions.passage: The origins of flags probably ①<u>began</u> with warriors decorating their spears with colored ribbons as a way of distinguishing one army from another. This practice was ②<u>adopted</u> by early explorers, who started using flags to show who newly discovered lands belonged to. During the modern era, flags ③<u>became</u> a symbol of individual nations, and it has become accepted that every country must have its own flag. Most of these national flags are roughly the same size and shape. They commonly feature bold colors and simple patterns, as flags with intricate patterns would appear ④<u>distort</u> when blowing in the wind.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: distort → distorted (appear + 과거분사: '~한 상태로 보이다')
det.analysis:
① began: 'The origins of flags probably began with ~' 과거시제 동사 — 적절해요.

② adopted: 'This practice was adopted by ~'는 'be동사 + 과거분사'의 수동태(~되었다)라 적절해요.

③ became: 'flags became a symbol'도 과거시제라 적절해요.

④ distort: 'would appear ___'에서 appear(~해 보이다) 뒤에는 상태를 나타내는 형용사나 과거분사가 와야 해요. '뒤틀린 상태로 보이다'라는 뜻이라 과거분사 distorted가 맞고, 동사원형 distort는 틀려요. ←정답
det.tip: appear + 과거분사(형용사 역할) = ~한 상태로 보이다. appear distorted

questions.passage: Around 2.35 billion years ago, Earth's atmosphere underwent a significant transition: It went from being oxygen-free to possessing a small percentage of oxygen. This change was partly due to tiny organisms ①<u>known</u> as cyanobacteria. Cyanobacteria, which evolved approximately 2.7 billion years ago, took in water to obtain hydrogen. This allowed them to ②<u>assimilating</u> carbon from CO₂ in the atmosphere. They then ③<u>released</u> oxygen as waste. But how could such tiny creatures have caused such a huge change in the planet? It is believed that the amount of oxygen cyanobacteria released slowly ④<u>increased</u> over hundreds of millions of years. Over this period, it accumulated in Earth's oceans, oxygenating the water. Eventually, the oceans' accumulated oxygen began to escape into the atmosphere. There, it reacted with methane, gradually displacing it. Had there been no cyanobacteria, oxygen might never have become a major component of Earth's atmosphere.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: assimilating → assimilate ('allow + 목적어 + to + 동사원형'이라 to 뒤는 동사원형)
det.analysis:
① known: 'organisms known as cyanobacteria(남세균으로 알려진 유기체)'로, 명사를 뒤에서 꾸미는 과거분사예요. 적절합니다.

② assimilating: 'This allowed them to ___ carbon'에서 'allow + 목적어(them) + to + 동사원형' 구문이에요. to 뒤에는 반드시 동사원형이 와야 하므로 assimilate가 맞아요. -ing형 assimilating은 틀려요 ←정답

③ released: 'They then released oxygen(그것들은 그런 다음 산소를 방출했다)' 주어 They에 대한 과거시제 본동사라 적절합니다.

④ increased: 'the amount of oxygen ... slowly increased' that절 안의 과거시제 본동사라 적절합니다.
det.tip: allow + 목적어 + to + 동사원형. allowed them to assimilate(그들이 흡수하게 했다)

questions.passage: Being alone makes us more creative. Many great artists and thinkers throughout history have lived by themselves. When we are alone, we have fewer distractions. This ①<u>allow</u> our thoughts to run free without interruption or judgment. Creative people have entire worlds inside their heads, and being alone gives them the opportunity to bring ideas from this inner world into the real world. Steve Wozniak, for example, invented the Apple computer sitting alone at a desk. He says his creativity came from being introverted as a child. Had it not been for his shyness, he might not have become a computer expert. However, this does not mean we should stop working together with others. Had it not been for Wozniak's collaboration with Steve Jobs, he could not have started his own business. Therefore, we should seek out solitude, but only when we need it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①은 어법상 틀렸다. 어법에 맞게 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: allow → allows: 주어 This(앞 내용을 가리키는 단수)에 맞는 단수동사 allows
det.analysis:
밑줄이 든 부분은 'This ___ our thoughts to run free(이것은 우리의 생각이 자유롭게 흐르도록 해 준다)'예요.

① 주어 This는 앞 문장 전체(혼자 있어 방해가 적다는 내용)를 하나로 가리키는 단수예요.

② 단수 주어에는 동사원형 allow가 아니라 -s가 붙은 단수동사 allows가 와야 해요. (allow: ~하도록 해 주다 → allows)
det.tip: 단수 주어 This → 단수동사 allows (allow 아님)

questions.passage: People often omit the period at the end of sentences in single-sentence text messages, which has influenced the way we perceive periods. In an experiment, participants reading text messages found single sentences with a period less sincere than those without one. This could be due to something called "situational code-switching," which simply means that __________. For example, the language that students use in the classroom is different from the language they use on the playground. If they talked to their friends the same way they talked to their teachers, it would probably sound strange. Similarly, a person using periods in text messages can cause feelings of awkwardness, just like someone using formal language in a casual setting.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸을 완성하시오. (10단어) (영어로)
'우리는 사회적 환경에 따라 말하는 방식을 바꾼다'
[조건] (1) change, depending, how, on, setting, social, talk, the, we, we를 모두 사용
(2) 10단어로 쓸 것
(3) 'depending on'을 사용할 것

det.korean: we change how we talk depending on the social setting = 우리는 사회적 환경에 따라 말하는 방식을 바꾼다
det.analysis:

'~에 따라'라는 뜻은 depending on으로 표현하고, 마지막에 the social setting(사회적 환경)을 붙여요.

순서: we + change + how + we + talk + depending + on + the + social + setting.
det.tip: we change(주어+동사) + how we talk(목적어) + depending on(~에 따라) + the social setting

questions.wa: we change how we talk depending on the social setting
accept: we change how we talk depending on the social setting

questions.passage: In the 1800s, the people of Ireland used potatoes as their basic food source. Unfortunately, everyone was growing the same type of potato, which meant the crops all had the same genes. The farmers did not realize the danger in this. In the 1840s, a new potato disease struck. The genetically identical potatoes all lacked the ability to fight the disease, so they all rotted. Because people were dependent mainly on potatoes for their food, Ireland suffered a famine in which one in eight people died during the following years. If people had grown many types of potatoes, they could have identified resistant ones and grown more of them, making the famine less serious. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①은 어법상 틀립니다. 어법에 맞게 고쳐 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: know → knowing (전치사 Despite 뒤에는 명사 역할을 하는 동명사가 와야 함)
det.analysis:
밑줄 문장은 'Despite ①know this, many countries today take the same risk(이것을 앎에도 불구하고 많은 나라가 여전히 같은 위험을 감수한다)'예요. Despite는 '~에도 불구하고'라는 뜻의 전치사예요. 전치사 뒤에는 명사나 명사 역할을 하는 말이 와야 하는데, 동사 know를 명사처럼 쓰려면 -ing를 붙인 동명사 knowing으로 바꿔야 해요. 동사원형 know는 전치사 뒤에 올 수 없으므로 틀려요.

know(X) → knowing(O, 전치사 뒤 동명사)
det.tip: 전치사(Despite) 뒤에는 동명사 → Despite knowing this

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸을 완성하시오. (8단어) (영어로)

questions.passage: Socotra Island, a small island ①<u>owned</u> by Yemen and located in the Arabian Sea, looks as if it were part of another planet. It is home to about 800 species of rare plants and animals, many of which are found nowhere else on earth. Because the island experiences extreme heat and frequent droughts, many of its plants have ③<u>evolved</u> unusual appearances. One striking example is the dragon's blood tree. Its branches make it look like a giant umbrella. It gets its name from a thick, red substance that ④<u>comes</u> out when its bark is cut. When this happens, it appears as if the tree were bleeding.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 어색한 것을 어법에 맞게 고쳐 쓰시오. (영어로, 한 단어)

det.korean: caused → causing (앞 절 전체를 받는 분사구문이므로 현재분사 causing)
det.analysis:
① owned: 'a small island owned by Yemen' 섬이 '소유되는' 수동 과거분사 후치수식 — 적절
